reviews.title: Full of disappointment
reviews.text:
After almost 10 years on Grindr, I was banned without a single specific reason. When I asked for an explanation, all I received was a generic statement about creating a “safe and authentic community.” Seriously? Is that your idea of transparency and accountability?

Grindr, your commitment to safety sounds impressive in a slogan. In reality, where is it when people genuinely need you?

In countries where being gay can mean facing blackmail, threats, persecution, or even physical violence, your platform can expose people to real danger. Yet users reaching out to your Help Center can be met with silence.

I personally reported several accounts that people in local communities had repeatedly flagged as fake and potentially dangerous. People warned each other that meeting these accounts could lead to serious trouble. Yet those profiles remained on Grindr, and some are still there today. Users have essentially had to warn one another and figure out for themselves whom to avoid because the platform they rely on for safety failed to give them confidence that their reports mattered. It is sad that the community has to protect itself while Grindr looks the other way.

And privacy? Grindr has faced serious criticism over user data and location privacy. For LGBTQ+ people living in hostile environments, exposing someone’s location can have devastating consequences. People’s safety and lives can be at stake. What meaningful protection do they receive when they desperately need help?

Mean

reviews.title: PLEASE FIX THE INBOX SCROLL BUG
reviews.text:
This bug has been going on for YEARS. Please fix it.

Every time I scroll down through my inbox to older conversations, open one, and then go back to my conversation list, Grindr automatically throws me ALL THE WAY back to the top of my inbox instead of keeping my previous scroll position.

So if I’m trying to go through several older conversations, I have to scroll all the way down again after EVERY SINGLE CHAT I open. It makes navigating your inbox ridiculously frustrating.

And this isn’t some new or isolated issue. The same problem was reported on Grindr’s own feedback platform back in March 2024, and it’s now 2026. I’ve also experienced it for well over a year despite countless app updates.

Other similar apps, including much newer ones, manage to preserve your position in a conversation list without any issue. This is basic app navigation.

Please stop ignoring this incredibly annoying bug and FIX THE CHAT INBOX SCROLL POSITION. After more than two years of public reports, users shouldn’t still be dealing with this.

reviews.title: Scammers and every update the interface gets worse
reviews.text:
Grindr has always had a scammer issue, but in the past month it’s gone off a cliff. I now get 20+ messages a day from scam accounts. And make no mistake, grindr could easily fix this but won’t because it inflates their “active user” interactions and count. Grindr doesn’t care if this hurts their most vulnerable users and could easily be destroying hundreds of lives, just as long as their profits margins go up. 

And Grindr has been laser focused on their profit margins the past year. The paid subscriptions on here are beyond overpriced at the cheapest plan being $60/mo and only offer extremely basic features. And without paying, you will see long, unskippable, full screen ads every 3 accounts or so. And remember, most the messages you’re getting are scammers, so you’re just wasting time and watching ads by having to report scammers.

Grindr has also made some insane interface decisions. Most recently, they now require you to have a paid subscription to see taps (a quick message/ Facebook poke) after an hour. So someone could have interacted with you and you’d never know because the tap expired. Literally just hiding your messages from you until you pay $60/mo!

reviews.title: The Downward Spiral
reviews.text: About 6 months before this review, the app was fine.  You’d get your occasional bot but it was manageable.  Reports somewhat worked and real guys were around.  Now, it’s clear the AI spam and bot machine has taken over.  Reporting spam, bots, endless streams of OF spammers, fake profiles, and impersonators go to a void that they don’t take serious or even look at.  I’m still waiting 3 months for obvious reports to get sorted.  I’ve done moderation and backend work, I know how it operates and there’s no excuse.  Returning spammers come back like nothing happened. Support is probably entirely AI.  If they respond (BIG if) they send brainless form letter responses that graze over any specifics of what you wrote about.  They aren’t listening.  Now the CEO says AI is their future and focus.  It’s time to take things elsewhere.  This used to be the place to be, not anymore.  The pay to play system has gotten greedy, and for what?  Worse of an app, exponentially more spam, far less access, and more brainless third-hand thinking AI slop?  The users minds are sinking with it.  It’s over, guys and it’s only going to get worse.  Sad stuff.

reviews.title: A Paid Membership That Shrinks by the Day
reviews.text:
This app introduces a new restriction almost every single day. I am currently using the Extra membership, yet the limits applied on the day you purchase the package and the limits applied towards the end of the subscription period are completely inconsistent. Previously, you could access everyone who had sent you a TAP, whether recently or at the start of the month, without any limits. Now you can only view four of them. The access area for anyone using the Extra package is becoming more and more restricted over time.

This situation is genuinely shocking and clearly disadvantages users. It is also legally questionable because the terms of a purchased package should not be altered arbitrarily while the subscription is still active. Despite this, Grindr introduces a new limitation almost every week, and at this point there is barely any difference left between Extra and Free.

In conclusion, this reflects poor management, a bleak approach, and a strategy that feels rather exploitative towards users
